subject.title: Trusted-proxy WebChat: per-user sender identity + per-user agent ACL - supported pattern?

question: Should trusted-proxy WebChat become a multi-user identity and per-agent authorization boundary, or should the documented supported pattern remain separate gateways or trust boundaries?
rationale: The current implementation treats trusted-proxy as gateway/operator authentication with allowUsers and scopes, while the request would add security-sensitive principal and agent-authorization semantics.

options.title: Design gateway-enforced ACLs
options.body: Add a maintained trusted-proxy identity model, documented config, server-side enforcement, and tests before recommending shared-team WebChat deployments.

options.title: Document single-boundary support
options.body: Keep runtime behavior as-is and explicitly document separate gateways or hosts for users who must not address each other's agents.

recommendation.title: Design gateway-enforced ACLs
recommendation.body: Add a maintained trusted-proxy identity model, documented config, server-side enforcement, and tests before recommending shared-team WebChat deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and commit metadata place this handle closest to the trusted-proxy WebSocket and chat.send surfaces that would need a security-boundary decision.
